chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

Whoever travels a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes him travel a path to Paradise. Surely, the angels lay down their wings for the seeker of knowledge, being pleased with him. And indeed, those in the heavens and on the earth seek forgiveness for the seeker of knowledge — even the whale in the sea. The virtue of the scholar over the worshiper is like the virtue of the full moon over the rest of the stars on the night of the full moon. And surely, the scholars are the inheritors of the prophets. Indeed, the prophets did not bequeath a dinar or a dirham, but rather they bequeathed knowledge — so whoever takes from it has taken an abundant share.

key_terms.الحوت في البحر: The whale in the sea — signifying that all of creation, even marine life, seeks forgiveness for the knowledge-seeker
key_terms.طالب العلم: Seeker of knowledge — one who pursues religious learning with sincerity
key_terms.ورثة الأنبياء: Inheritors of the prophets — the scholars who carry prophetic knowledge forward

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet Muhammad say about the virtue of seeking knowledge and the status of scholars in Islam?
ai.summary: This is one of the most celebrated prophetic traditions on the virtue of seeking knowledge, narrated through the chain of Imams back to the Prophet Muhammad. Delivered during an assembly in Ramadan 367 AH, it establishes that seeking religious knowledge is a path to Paradise, that all of creation — from angels to sea creatures — prays for the knowledge-seeker, and that scholars surpass mere worshipers just as the full moon outshines the stars. The hadith culminates in declaring scholars as the true heirs of the prophets, since prophets bequeathed knowledge rather than material wealth.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from Abdullah b. Maymun from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said: Whoever travels a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes him travel a path to Paradise. Surely, the angels put their wings on a seeker of knowledge that they become pleased with. Those in the heavens and the Earth - even the whales in the ocean - seek forgiveness for the seekers of knowledge. The virtue of the scholar over the worshiper is like that of the full moon over the stars. The scholars are the inheritors of the prophets, for the prophets do not bequeath gold or silver, but they bequeath knowledge - whoever takes from it has taken an abundant omen.
